title: The Borrowed Clock
premise: In the winter of 1917, Ulyana Iversen, a battlefield nurse who secretly records the names of the fallen that officers omit from their reports, receives a sealed letter from a dying colonel: inside is proof that the Vasiliev family — neighbors from his childhood, now declared enemy — are to be scapegoated for a supply scandal that reaches into army command. Bound by a peacetime promise to Elena Vasiliev, Ulyana abandons the safety of his post and travels through a collapsing front with the colonel's ledger and his own, hunted by a major who needs the Vasilievs convicted before the armistice erases the crime. He reaches them too late to save their home but in time to save their lives, and at a military tribunal he trades his own name and standing for theirs, reading aloud the names the army tried to forget. The book ends with the family exiled but alive, Ulyana stripped of rank yet carrying a new ledger — one the Vasilievs keep for him, of everyone who helped.
about_author: Quentin Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing field hospital records from the Eastern Front. He writes from a farmhouse in Norfolk, where he still keeps a broken clock that belonged to a stranger.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Ulyana Iversen, a field nurse at a dressing station near Riga, tends the wounded by day and, by candlelight, records in his private ledger the names officers omit from casualty reports. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: quiet defiance — the small dignity of remembering the forgotten.

chapters.title: A Letter Sealed in Wax
chapters.summary: Colonel Brandt, dying of a wound Ulyana cannot mend, presses a sealed letter into his hands and makes him swear to deliver it to the Vasiliev family in Krasnogorsk. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: dread and honor entwined — a promise made to a man who will not survive to see it kept.

chapters.title: What the Major Wanted Buried
chapters.summary: Major Reinholt arrives to inventory the station and notices Ulyana's habit of asking questions about the dead. He offers promotion for silence. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the first open threat — kindness with a knife behind it.

chapters.title: The Road East
chapters.summary: Ulyana deserts his post under cover of a supply run, carrying Brandt's letter sewn into his coat. He travels with a convoy of refugees, measuring the world again in what can be carried. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into purpose — no way back.

chapters.title: The Girl on the Train
chapters.summary: On a crowded troop train, Ulyana meets Marta, a teenage courier who smuggles letters for displaced families. She guesses what he carries and offers the back roads in exchange for a place in his ledger of the remembered. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance — trust offered in a world that punishes it.

chapters.title: Krasnogorsk in Winter
chapters.summary: Ulyana reaches Krasnogorsk and finds the Vasiliev house under guard, the family confined pending a tribunal for the supply scandal. He watches from the churchyard where he and Elena once played. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: homecoming turned to grief — the past visible but untouchable.

chapters.title: Elena's Bargain
chapters.summary: Through Marta's courier network, Ulyana passes the letter to Elena Vasiliev, who reveals Brandt's proof names Major Reinholt's patron, General Hess, as the true thief. Elena refuses to flee and abandon the townspeople who depend on her. POV: Elena. Emotional beat: stubborn courage — a woman who will not be made a ghost in her own story.

chapters.title: The Ledger of the Living
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Elena combine his ledger of the dead with her list of witnesses: farmers, clerks, and soldiers who can testify Hess orchestrated the theft. Marta begins carrying summons. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: hope as an act of logistics — justice assembled name by name.

chapters.title: Reinholt's Net
chapters.summary: Reinholt, tipped off by a frightened witness, arrests two of Elena's contacts and posts a description of a nurse traveling with forged papers. Ulyana burns his identity documents. POV: Reinholt. Emotional beat: the hunter's cold certainty — and a first hairline crack of doubt about his patron.

chapters.title: The Chapel Cellar
chapters.summary: The witnesses hide in the chapel cellar while Reinholt's men search the town. Ulyana, disguised as a gravedigger, walks past the major at the gate. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: terror held still — courage as the ability to keep walking.

chapters.title: A Name Struck Through
chapters.summary: Reinholt interrogates the arrested witnesses; one, an old schoolmaster, dies under questioning before speaking. Ulyana adds the schoolmaster to his ledger and Elena, for the first time, wavers. POV: Elena. Emotional beat: grief and fury — the cost of resistance made flesh.

chapters.title: The Armistice Rumor
chapters.summary: News spreads that an armistice may come within weeks, which would dissolve the tribunal and erase the crime — unless Hess secures a conviction first. Reinholt is ordered to accelerate. POV: Reinholt. Emotional beat: desperation on both sides — the clock now audible to everyone.

chapters.title: Marta's Long Night
chapters.summary: Marta carries the final witness summons through a checkpoint by hiding the papers in a broken clock she claims to be delivering for repair. She is detained, questioned, and released on a child's lie. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into pride — the smallest courier carries the heaviest hour.

chapters.title: Hess Arrives
chapters.summary: General Hess comes to Krasnogorsk in person, charming the town by day while ordering the witnesses' arrest by night. Ulyana recognizes him from Brandt's description and realizes the tribunal is a stage play already written. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the mask of authority seen through — and the loneliness of being the only one looking.

chapters.title: What Brandt Knew
chapters.summary: A second letter from Brandt, held by a chaplain, surfaces: it names the exact convoy and dates of the stolen supplies, enough to convict — if it reaches the tribunal's one honest officer, Judge Lindqvist. POV: Elena. Emotional beat: a door opening in a wall — proof that the machine has a seam.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: One of the cellar witnesses, broken by fear for his family, tells Reinholt where the letter is hidden. The chapel is raided; Ulyana escapes with the papers but Marta is taken. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: betrayal without hatred — he understands the man who broke, and grieves anyway.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Reinholt offers a trade: the letter for Marta. Ulyana agrees, then substitutes a copy, keeping the original and losing the element of surprise. Marta returns changed, silent about what she endured. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: rescue and its residue — freedom that does not feel like victory.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Opens
chapters.summary: The Vasiliev trial begins in the town hall. Hess's case is seamless until Ulyana, in nurse's whites, walks in and requests to testify as keeper of the casualty records. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the point of no return — a man volunteering his own destruction.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Names
chapters.summary: Ulyana reads aloud the ledger: the dead the officers omitted, the convoy dates, the witnesses, the schoolmaster who died asking nothing. The room goes still; Judge Lindqvist accepts the ledger into evidence over Hess's objection. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: climax — memory itself placed on the scales of justice, and tipping them.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Reinholt, confronted with Brandt's second letter, breaks and turns witness against Hess. The charges against the Vasilievs are dismissed; Hess is ordered arrested but dies by his own hand before the cell closes. POV: Reinholt. Emotional beat: the collapse of a loyal man — justice arriving, imperfect and late.

chapters.title: Exile, Lightly Carried
chapters.summary: The Vasilievs, though cleared, cannot remain; they choose exile together rather than stay in a town that watched. Elena asks Ulyana to come, but his name is struck from the registers and his future is elsewhere. POV: Elena. Emotional beat: bittersweet parting — belonging redefined as the people, not the place.

chapters.title: The Clock Keeps Time
chapters.summary: At the station, Marta gives Ulyana the broken clock from the checkpoint, repaired by the watchmaker she once deceived. The Vasilievs board the train east; Ulyana opens a new ledger whose first page bears their names, written as living. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: resolution — time borrowed is time kept, and memory is the home no order can confiscate.
